A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same INTERSORT study. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated algorithms and renumbered figures.

before.justification: V2 reports original graph simulations and causal-ordering experiments on linear, RFF, neural-network, and simulated gene-expression data, including appendix results.

after.justification: V3 retains original simulations and adds intervention-selection experiments, runtime measurements, and an original INTERSORT analysis of the Sachs dataset.

M1.justification: The score formula, Wasserstein distances, SORTRANKING initialization, and LOCALSEARCH procedure remain unchanged, including their pseudocode. The confounder extension and selection-policy experiments introduce no modified ordering algorithm. The revised mathematical condition on c is assessed under T1.

E1.justification: V3 adds real human-cell flow-cytometry data from Sachs et al. in Appendix F.3, extending evaluation beyond simulations. It removes v2 Figure 7's finite-sample scale-free benchmarks across four data domains at 10 and 30 variables. Separate scale-free graph simulations in Figures 3–4 remain.

E2.justification: PC, GIES, DCDI, and EASE remain the comparison algorithms in corresponding benchmarks and also appear in the new runtime comparison. The intervention-selection experiment varies INTERSORT's settings, while the Sachs example has no competing algorithm. Removing an entire scale-free benchmark does not change comparator membership within retained experiments.

E3.justification: V3 introduces fixed-budget selection of 10 among 30 variables using most-children, random, and fewest-children policies; runtime and 30-versus-10-variable timing ratios; and a Sachs evaluation using 1,755 observational plus 4,091 interventional measurements with epsilon = 1.5. These substantially extend evaluation procedures. Corresponding synthetic benchmarks retain their sample budgets, normalization, settings, and Dtop metric.

E4.justification: Appendix F adds analyses of intervention-target selection (Figure 6), computational scaling across variable counts and intervention fractions (Figure 9), and a real-data ordering that identifies three incorrectly oriented reference edges (Figure 10). These address practical questions absent from v2's existing approximation and simulation analyses.

E5.justification: Matched experiments retain their stated repetition counts, including 20 graphs with 10 intervention configurations and benchmarking on 10 simulated datasets. The existing 95% confidence-interval discussion is unchanged. New plots include error bars or bands but disclose no different statistical estimation procedure, seed policy, or repetition count.

E6.justification: Shared benchmark plots retain identical results, including v2 Figure 6 renumbered as v3 Figure 7. New results show lower ordering error when selecting variables with more children, report runtime comparisons, and give Sachs Dtop = 3 against a 17-edge reference network. V2's eight-panel scale-free benchmark results are removed. These are additions and removals, not same-setting performance improvements.

T1.justification: New Section 5 introduces latent projections and Proposition 1, with an argument that interventional faithfulness survives marginalization to the directed part of an ADMG. This extends the theoretical treatment beyond causal sufficiency. The condition preceding Equation (1) also changes from c > 0 to c > epsilon. Existing theorems and appendix proofs otherwise remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract narrows the novelty formulation from introducing the notion of interventional faithfulness to introducing a novel variant. The principal contributions—an ordering score, theoretical error guarantees, and INTERSORT's empirical performance—remain substantially unchanged.

C2.justification: V3 explicitly extends applicability to observed subsets with latent confounders, while requiring stable confounders and absence of selection bias. Figure 6 additionally motivates estimating connectivity to choose intervention targets. These materially expand the applicability boundaries and practical interpretation beyond v2.

D1.justification: The Sachs example documents its sample composition, intervention count, Wasserstein distance, and epsilon = 1.5; Figure 9 adds computational-cost information. Existing simulator specifications, software versions and licenses, pseudocode, and hardware disclosures are retained. No new code-access provision is introduced.

R1.justification: Section 2 replaces the first-algorithm claim with an explicit comparison to Tian and Pearl, positioning the contribution around score optimization and partial-intervention guarantees. That work was already cited in v2; its 2013-to-2001 bibliographic update alone is not a new citation. V3 also substantially expands discussion of intervention-identification and latent-variable literature.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and proofs are retained. Local revisions expand related work and SCM/score explanations, add a latent-confounder section and appendix navigation, move Algorithm 1 into Appendix C, and correct wording such as three versus four baselines. Author affiliations and publication headers also change.

P2.justification: The appendix presentation changes substantially: v3 adds intervention-policy bars, a three-panel logarithmic runtime figure, and a causal-order diagram highlighting erroneous edges, while removing v2's eight-panel scale-free comparison. Algorithms are consolidated in Appendix C, tables and figures are repositioned, and ICLR formatting is adopted. Retained plot graphics remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: V3 provides a limited net improvement through clearer prior-work attribution, a formal treatment of latent confounders, and new selection, runtime, and real-data evidence. These gains are moderated by removing v2's scale-free benchmark comparison and by the Sachs example lacking baseline comparisons. The new c > epsilon condition also remains unreconciled with the retained single-cell settings c = epsilon = 0.5.
